runs.summary: I reviewed the DIFC employment contract against the listed DIFC Employment Law and data protection requirements. The contract has multiple direct compliance issues, including invalid probation and notice terms, excessive working hours, insufficient annual leave, missing DEWS provisions, incomplete anti-discrimination protections, and inadequate employee data protection language. It also omits several mandatory written employment particulars such as sick leave provisions and policy references.

findings.title: Missing required particulars
findings.description: The contract does not include all mandatory DIFC written employment statement items, including sick leave provisions, references to applicable policies, and a job description beyond the job title.

findings.title: Invalid probation terms
findings.description: The contract sets a nine-month probation period and only three days’ notice during probation, while DIFC permits a maximum six-month probation period and requires at least seven days’ written notice or payment in lieu.

findings.title: DEWS omitted
findings.description: The contract provides a traditional end-of-service payment instead of mandatory DEWS or qualifying scheme enrollment with monthly employer contributions at the required rates.

findings.title: Insufficient termination notice
findings.description: The contract provides 14 days’ notice regardless of length of service, conflicting with DIFC minimums of 30 days for under five years’ service and 90 days for five or more years. It also does not require written reasons for termination.

findings.title: Excessive working hours
findings.description: The contract states a 50-hour workweek and a 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM workday with only a 30-minute lunch break, exceeding the DIFC limit of 8 hours per day or 40 hours per week exclusive of breaks. It also omits the required Ramadan reduction for Muslim employees.

findings.title: Anti-discrimination policy missing
findings.description: The equal opportunity wording is too general and does not prohibit discrimination on the required protected grounds, provide an accessible written policy, or set out a formal complaints procedure for harassment including sexual harassment.

findings.title: Annual leave too low
findings.description: The contract provides only 15 working days of annual leave, below the DIFC minimum of 20 working days after 90 days of service. It also states unused leave cannot be carried forward, conflicting with the requirement that carry-forward be allowed subject to policy and used within 12 months.

findings.title: Data protections missing
findings.description: The contract permits the employer to process and transfer personal data worldwide as it deems necessary, without specifying a lawful basis, privacy notice, data minimisation, security measures, transfer safeguards, or employee rights.

runs.summary: I reviewed the DMCC employment contract against the listed DMCC employment regulations and UAE written contract requirements. The contract contains multiple direct conflicts with mandatory rules, including discretionary medical insurance, excessive working hours, inadequate notice, employee-paid repatriation, and reduced gratuity. It also omits several required administrative and formal contract requirements, including DMCC registration details and Arabic/bilingual execution. I reviewed the DMCC employment contract against the listed UAE labour-law employment terms. The contract contains multiple direct conflicts with required rules, including excessive probation, working hours, lack of overtime pay, reduced leave and sick leave, underpaid gratuity, short termination notice, and incomplete wage-payment safeguards. All listed clauses are applicable to this employment contract and each resulted in a compliance issue. I checked the contract against the DMCC accommodation allowance rule and the UAE non-compete requirements. The housing provision is acceptable because the contract states no separate housing benefit is provided. The non-compete clause has issues: it lacks required legal carve-outs and is drafted broadly rather than being clearly limited to genuinely competitive work.

findings.title: Missing DMCC registration
findings.description: The contract does not state that it must be registered with the DMCC Authority within 14 days of execution, and it does not include the employee DMCC access card number or a confirmation of DMCC employment rules compliance.

findings.title: Discretionary medical insurance
findings.description: The contract makes medical insurance optional and requires the employee to secure their own insurance until the company chooses to provide it.

findings.title: Visa costs deducted
findings.description: The contract says the company will sponsor the visa but allows visa costs to be deducted from the employee’s salary and omits the 60-day filing deadline and continuing valid-status obligation.

findings.title: Excessive weekly hours
findings.description: The contract requires 50 hours per week and allows further overtime, exceeding the DMCC cap of 48 hours including overtime and omitting Ramadan reduced hours.

findings.title: Insufficient notice period
findings.description: The contract allows termination on 14 days’ written notice and does not include the DMCC requirements for 30/90 days’ notice, notice delivery to DMCC, job-search time, or visa cancellation within 30 days of the last working day.

findings.title: Employee repatriation costs
findings.description: The contract states that the employee is solely responsible for all repatriation costs, contrary to the DMCC employer’s obligation to pay a one-way economy ticket unless the employee secures new UAE employment within 30 days.

findings.title: Understated gratuity
findings.description: The contract sets gratuity at 14 days’ basic salary per year and denies gratuity on resignation before three years, rather than following UAE Federal Labour Law and paying within 14 days of the last working day.

findings.title: Missing required particulars
findings.description: The contract is not shown as Arabic or bilingual, does not state it is executed in duplicate, and omits required details including employer address, employee date of birth, Emirates ID number, and job description/category.

findings.title: Excessive probation period
findings.description: The contract sets a 12-month probation period and permits immediate termination without notice. UAE labour requirements limit probation to six months and require 14 days’ written notice for employer termination during probation.

findings.title: Excessive working hours
findings.description: The contract requires 50 hours per week, exceeding the 48-hour weekly limit for adult employees. It also does not provide for Ramadan reduction or a break of at least one hour after no more than five consecutive working hours.

findings.title: No overtime pay
findings.description: The contract states that overtime may be required with no additional compensation. Mandatory rules require overtime pay at the applicable premium rates and limit overtime generally to two additional hours per day.

findings.title: Insufficient annual leave
findings.description: The annual leave entitlement is only 15 working days per year, below the required minimum of 30 calendar days after one year of service. The contract also omits the statutory entitlement for employees with six months but less than one year of service and the requirement to pay leave salary in advance.

findings.title: Insufficient sick leave
findings.description: The contract allows only up to 15 days of sick leave at the Company’s discretion. Required sick leave after probation is up to 90 days per year, with the first 15 days at full pay, next 30 days at half pay, and the remainder unpaid, subject to notice and medical certificate requirements.

findings.title: Reduced gratuity entitlement
findings.description: The contract calculates gratuity at only 14 days of basic salary per year and denies gratuity if the employee resigns before three years. The required entitlement starts after one year of continuous service and is calculated at 21 days of basic salary for each of the first five years and 30 days for each additional year, subject to the statutory cap and resignation reductions where applicable.

findings.title: Short termination notice
findings.description: The contract permits termination on 14 days’ written notice, which is below the required minimum of 30 calendar days. It also does not state that the employee receives full remuneration and continues duties during notice, or that the employer must grant at least one unpaid day per week for job searching.

findings.title: Wage payment gaps
findings.description: The contract states the salary in AED but does not require payment through approved financial institutions/WPS or payment within 10 days of the due date. It also allows visa costs to be deducted from the employee’s first three months’ salary without a stated cap consistent with wage-deduction limits.

findings.title: Broad non-compete scope
findings.description: The clause restricts all competing activities in the UAE without tying the restriction to the Company’s specific business, the employee’s role, or genuinely competitive work.

runs.summary: I reviewed the DMCC shareholders’ agreement against the specified DMCCA Company Regulations clauses. The main issues are unapproved currency/crypto-denominated share issuance, bypassing Registrar-related Articles procedures, and incomplete treatment of Licence suspension, termination and pre-licence consequences. Branch, name-change, and continuation provisions were treated as not applicable because this document does not address those matters. I reviewed the shareholders’ agreement against the DMCCA Company Regulations clauses on shares, capital changes, transfers/registers, distributions, cross-holdings and directors. The main issues are direct conflicts on bearer shares, share transfers, capital reductions, unapproved share denominations and director eligibility. The dividend and register provisions also omit several statutory safeguards that should be added to reduce compliance risk. I reviewed the DMCC shareholders' agreement against the specified DMCCA Company Regulations provisions on officers, meetings, accounts, audit and inspection/compliance powers. The agreement contains several direct conflicts, including Director financial assistance, no Company Secretary, incorrect AGM timing, US GAAP accounting, an excessive first financial year and shortened record retention. It also omits multiple required mechanisms for officer disqualification, shareholder meeting rights, financial reporting, auditor protections and DMCCA inspection/compliance directions. I reviewed the DMCC shareholders’ agreement against the listed DMCCA Company Regulations clauses on amalgamation, insolvency/winding-up, sanctions, licensing and contraventions. The agreement contains only limited winding-up and licence suspension wording and omits many mandatory statutory procedures, filings, notices and remedies. It also includes broad arbitration language that may conflict with statutory Court remedies for unfair prejudice. I reviewed the DMCC shareholders’ agreement against the listed DMCCA disclosure/false-information and voluntary licence suspension requirements. The agreement contains a basic disclosure clause, but several mandatory C33 elements are missing, including auditor reporting, anti-retaliation, anti-hindrance, false-information, and Registrar-direction obligations. The licence suspension language is also incomplete for voluntary suspension because it does not address shareholder approval, duration limits, or dormant-company rules.

findings.title: Unapproved share currency
findings.description: The agreement allows the Board to issue additional shares in any currency, including cryptocurrency-denominated tokens, without Registrar approval. C2 requires share capital to be denominated in UAE Dirhams or another currency approved by the Registrar.

findings.title: Articles process bypassed
findings.description: The agreement is supplemental to the Articles but permits additional share issuance without Registrar approval. Because C3 requires Articles to contain share capital information and new Articles to take effect on registration by the Registrar, the agreement should not bypass required Article amendment and filing steps.

findings.title: Licence consequences omitted
findings.description: The licence clause does not state that liabilities or commitments before the first Licence, or during Licence suspension or termination, are treated as shareholder liabilities. It also omits the risk that failure to obtain a Licence within 24 weeks of registration may lead to strike-off and dissolution.

findings.title: Register bypassed
findings.description: The agreement allows bearer shares to be transferred by delivery without registration or Registrar notification. This conflicts with the requirement that shareholder status depends on acquisition/agreement plus entry in the Shareholder Register.

findings.title: Unapproved share currency
findings.description: The agreement permits additional shares in any Board-selected currency, including cryptocurrency-denominated tokens, without Registrar approval. Share capital must be denominated in UAE Dirhams or another currency approved by the Registrar.

findings.title: Invalid capital reduction
findings.description: The agreement states that share capital reduction takes effect immediately without Registrar notice, publication, or director solvency certificate. DMCC rules require a Special Resolution plus specified notice/publication and a director certificate on solvency or creditor consent.

findings.title: Bearer shares prohibited
findings.description: The agreement requires the Company to issue bearer share certificates. This is a direct breach of the DMCC prohibition on bearer shares.

findings.title: Defective transfer procedure
findings.description: The transfer clause says only the transferor must sign and that delivery to the Registrar is enough. DMCC rules require a share transfer document signed by or on behalf of both transferor and transferee and delivered to both the Registrar and the Company.

findings.title: Registers omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not require the Company to maintain required registers, take precautions for the Minutes Register, provide security-interest details to the Registrar within five Business Days, or preserve inspection/rectification rights.

findings.title: Distribution safeguards incomplete
findings.description: The agreement does not state that directors must approve distributions by simple majority, does not cover all required assessment factors and undistributable reserves, and does not include shareholder repayment liability for unlawful distributions, including non-cash distributions.

findings.title: Invalid director qualifications
findings.description: The agreement sets the minimum director age at 16 instead of 18, uses a five-year dishonesty lookback instead of ten years, allows non-natural person directors by shareholder agreement rather than Registrar approval, and omits other disqualification grounds.

findings.title: Unqualified alternates allowed
findings.description: The agreement allows an alternate director to avoid the qualification requirements. DMCC rules require an alternate director to meet the director qualification criteria.

findings.title: Director filings missing
findings.description: The agreement does not require notification to the Registrar within fourteen Business Days for director changes or removal within ten Business Days where a director ceases to meet qualification criteria.

findings.title: Director loans allowed
findings.description: The agreement allows loans, advances, guarantees or other financial assistance to Directors, subject only to a cap and shareholder approval. C17 prohibits the Company from providing financial assistance to a Director.

findings.title: Continuing duties narrowed
findings.description: The agreement preserves only duties regarding confidential information and opportunities. C17 also preserves duties regarding exploitation of property, information or opportunities and duties relating to things done or omitted before the Director ceased to serve.

findings.title: Secretary disclaimed
findings.description: The agreement says the Company is not required to appoint a Company Secretary. C18 requires every Company to have a Secretary, with appointment by Directors, qualification rules, removal/replacement obligations, Registrar notification and filing responsibilities.

findings.title: Manager notice wrong
findings.description: The agreement provides a 14-Business-Day notice period for Manager changes. C19 requires notice to the Registrar within 5 Business Days when the Manager resigns, is removed, dies or is incapacitated, and also requires appointment by Directors' resolution.

findings.title: Officer rules omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not address third-party assumptions about publicly listed Officers, Officers' duty to procure regulatory filings on time, Registrar/DMCCA disqualification orders, or mandatory removal of disqualified Directors, Secretaries or Managers within 10 Business Days.

findings.title: AGM timing excessive
findings.description: The agreement allows the first AGM within 36 months and later AGMs every 18 months. C21 requires the first annual General Meeting within 18 months from registration and once every 12 months thereafter, unless the Articles provide a shorter period.

findings.title: Notice period short
findings.description: The agreement permits General Meetings on 8 Business Days' notice and omits required notice contents such as proposed Ordinary or Special Resolution contents and relevant accounts and auditor reports.

findings.title: Quorum too low
findings.description: The agreement sets quorum at not less than 50% of voting rights. C21's default quorum requires persons holding more than 50% of total voting rights unless the Articles provide otherwise.

findings.title: Written resolutions invalid
findings.description: The agreement allows written resolutions signed by 75% of voting rights. C21 requires written resolutions to be signed by all entitled Shareholders to have the same effect as resolutions passed at a General Meeting.

findings.title: Meeting rights omitted
findings.description: The agreement omits the right of shareholders holding 10% or more of share capital to request an extraordinary General Meeting, the related calling timetable, and the requirement to maintain an inspectable Minutes Register at the registered office.

findings.title: Non-IFRS accounts
findings.description: The agreement requires accounts to be prepared under US GAAP. C22 requires accounts to be prepared in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards.

findings.title: Financial year excessive
findings.description: The agreement sets the first financial year at 24 months from registration. C22 requires the first financial year to be at least 6 months and not longer than 18 months.

findings.title: Records retained briefly
findings.description: The agreement preserves accounting records for only 3 years. C22 requires accounting records to be preserved for at least 5 years, or 15 years for records relating to real estate.

findings.title: Reporting process omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not require accounts to be prepared and approved within 6 months after financial year-end, examined by a DMCCA-approved auditor, laid before a General Meeting with the auditor's report, and filed with the Registrar within 5 Business Days of that meeting.

findings.title: Audit appointment incomplete
findings.description: The agreement requires a DMCCA-approved auditor but does not require appointment at a General Meeting, written consent, absence of precluding matters, auditor removal by Ordinary Resolution, or all required report statements including IFRS compliance and DMCCA-required matters.

findings.title: Auditor protections omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not address the auditor's right to access records and obtain explanations, required audit investigations, prohibitions on false or misleading statements, concealment, coercion or denial of access, or the auditor's cessation statement.

findings.title: Inspection powers omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not provide for DMCCA-appointed inspectors' powers to investigate, require attendance, obtain documents and information, or for Registrar directions and DMCCA orders to remedy regulatory non-compliance.

findings.title: Amalgamation missing
findings.description: The agreement does not include the required DMCC amalgamation framework, including Registrar consent, authorisations for Non-DMCC entities, shareholder/director approvals, officer declarations on solvency and assets, creditor prejudice protections, and non-appealability of refusal.

findings.title: Pre-insolvency reports omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not require Directors to report to the Registrar within ten Business Days if the Company’s purpose has expired or business ceased, liabilities exceed assets, or employees remain unpaid for three consecutive months.

findings.title: Loss notice omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not require the Company to notify Shareholders within twenty-one days after becoming aware that losses have reached 75% or more of Share Capital.

findings.title: Winding-up effects omitted
findings.description: The agreement only addresses unanimous voluntary winding-up and does not cover solvent, summary, insolvent or court winding-up, Federal bankruptcy law applicability, winding-up under the Articles or due to 75% losses, cessation of business, continuation of powers, or void share transfers after commencement.

findings.title: Solvency declaration incomplete
findings.description: The agreement requires a declaration of solvency but does not require Directors to make full inquiry and state whether the Company has no assets/no liabilities, assets/no liabilities, or liabilities that will be discharged in full within twelve months.

findings.title: Filing duties omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not require the Company to appoint liquidators at a General Meeting or send the notice of appointment, declaration and meeting minutes to the Registrar within fifteen Business Days.

findings.title: Summary process omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not address summary winding-up, including the declaration that the Company has no assets/no liabilities or assets/no liabilities, final winding-up within six months, and conversion to solvent or insolvent winding-up where required.

findings.title: Liquidator reports omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not state that Directors’ powers cease on liquidator appointment, that annual progress reports must be prepared if the winding-up exceeds twelve months, or that a final summary, final General Meeting and Registrar submissions are required before dissolution.

findings.title: Insolvent process missing
findings.description: The agreement does not require a General Meeting resolution, a Creditors’ meeting within ten Business Days, notices to Creditors at least eight Business Days before the meeting, appointment of a chairman, proposed liquidators, or a statement of affairs signed by at least one Director.

findings.title: Committee rules omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not provide for Creditors appointing a Liquidation Committee of three to five eligible members, liquidator reporting to that Committee, six-monthly Committee meetings, or annual Company and Creditors’ meetings if winding-up exceeds twelve months.

findings.title: Court winding-up omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not address involuntary winding-up by the Court on a Registrar petition where the Company is struck off or seriously/repeatedly contravenes the Regulations, including court identification of the liquidator and commencement from the petition date.

findings.title: Liquidation statement missing
findings.description: The agreement does not require every document issued by the Company in winding-up to state that the Company is in liquidation.

findings.title: Priority wording incomplete
findings.description: The agreement lists secured creditors in the priority waterfall but does not limit payment to secured creditors to the extent of their security, as required by the Regulations.

findings.title: Liquidator powers omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not state the liquidator’s powers to pay creditors, compromise claims, bring or defend proceedings, call meetings, carry on business for beneficial winding-up, sell property, execute documents, draw bills, raise secured money or appoint agents.

findings.title: Distribution rules missing
findings.description: The agreement does not require property to be realised and applied pari passu among liabilities subject to the statutory priority, nor distribution of remaining property among Shareholders according to their rights and interests.

findings.title: Cooperation duties omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not require current or former Officers, management employees or liquidators to comply with reasonable requests and directions of the liquidator, or prohibit hindering or obstructing the liquidator.

findings.title: Records rules omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not state that dissolution occurs upon Registrar confirmation, how remaining property and records are disposed of in solvent/summary versus insolvent winding-up, or the ten-year records responsibility rule.

findings.title: Sanctions missing
findings.description: The agreement does not address that DMCCA may impose sanctions for contraventions, including service restrictions, fines, licence suspension or termination, strike-off, or other sanctions deemed appropriate by DMCCA.

findings.title: Suspension grounds incomplete
findings.description: The agreement states the Company must cease operations during licence suspension, but it does not list the statutory suspension grounds, including ceasing business for more than three months, non-compliance, unlicensed/restricted activities, unpaid amounts, reputational protection, or related-company suspension.

findings.title: Termination rules missing
findings.description: The agreement does not address DMCCA licence termination grounds or the requirement to immediately cease operations and close premises upon receiving a Termination Notice.

findings.title: Strike-off omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not address Strike Off Notices, response periods, public notice, continuing Officer and Shareholder liability, personal liability for persons purporting to bind a struck-off Company, or the requirement for Shareholders to immediately commence winding-up proceedings.

findings.title: Contravention liability missing
findings.description: The agreement includes a disclosure obligation but does not state that doing prohibited acts, failing required acts, or otherwise contravening the Regulations is a contravention, nor that persons knowingly concerned and officeholders/corporate entities may also commit contraventions.

findings.title: Unfair prejudice omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not recognise Shareholders’ statutory right to apply to the Court for relief if the Company’s affairs are conducted in a manner unfairly prejudicial to one or more Shareholders.

findings.title: Court remedies conflicted
findings.description: The arbitration clause broadly requires any dispute to be finally resolved by arbitration, without carving out statutory applications to the Court for unfair prejudice relief under the Regulations.

findings.title: Disclosure scope incomplete
findings.description: The disclosure obligation is limited to contraventions or likely contraventions and does not expressly cover failures or likely failures to comply with any obligation, or other matters prescribed by DMCCA attributable to the Company, Officers, or Representatives.

findings.title: Auditor reporting omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not address the auditor’s obligation to disclose reportable matters to the Registrar, except where privileged communications are involved.

findings.title: Protections omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not state that provisions hindering regulatory disclosure are void or that no person may suffer detriment for giving information or documents to DMCCA or the Registrar in good faith.

findings.title: False information omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not prohibit providing false, misleading, or deceptive information to DMCCA or the Registrar, or concealing information where concealment is likely to mislead or deceive them.

findings.title: Registrar directions omitted
findings.description: The agreement does not require parties to comply with orders, directions, or requirements issued under the Regulations, or acknowledge that the Registrar may require communications in English or Arabic.

findings.title: Suspension procedure incomplete
findings.description: The agreement addresses suspension consequences but does not specify that voluntary suspension requires Ordinary Resolution approval, is limited to up to twelve months unless the Registrar approves longer, and remains subject to DMCCA/Registrar dormant-company rules.

runs.summary: I reviewed the UAE mainland employment agreement against the listed Federal Labour Law employment-term requirements. The agreement contains multiple direct conflicts with mandatory rules, including excessive probation and working hours, waiver of overtime, inadequate annual and sick leave, denial of gratuity, and too-short termination notice. It also omits required written-contract particulars and is not presented in Arabic or bilingual form. I checked the UAE mainland employment contract against the listed wage-payment and non-compete requirements. The salary clause states AED monthly payment by bank transfer, but it does not commit to WPS/approved financial-institution payment. The non-compete clause raises multiple issues because it exceeds two years, covers the entire MENA region, is not limited to genuinely competitive work, and omits required statutory exceptions.

findings.title: Required particulars missing
findings.description: The contract is not presented in Arabic or bilingual form and does not include all mandatory particulars, including a full employer address, employee date of birth, job category, workplace location, duplicate-copy statement, and compliant termination notice details.

findings.title: Probation exceeds limit
findings.description: The probation clause exceeds the six-month statutory maximum and allows termination during probation without the required 14 days' written notice.

findings.title: Working hours excessive
findings.description: The agreement requires 10 hours per day and 60 hours per week, which exceeds the ordinary maximum of 8 hours per day and 48 hours per week, and it does not include the Ramadan two-hour daily reduction or the required break after five consecutive hours.

findings.title: Overtime pay waived
findings.description: The agreement says no additional compensation is payable for hours beyond the schedule and purports to waive overtime rights, contrary to the required overtime premium rules.

findings.title: Annual leave underpaid
findings.description: The agreement provides only 20 calendar days after one year and states that no leave accrues during the first year, conflicting with the statutory 30 calendar days after one year and two days per month after six months but less than one year.

findings.title: Sick leave discretionary
findings.description: The agreement makes sick leave subject to the employer's sole discretion and omits the required entitlement of up to 90 days per year after probation with the statutory full-pay, half-pay, and unpaid periods.

findings.title: Gratuity denied
findings.description: The agreement states that no end-of-service gratuity or severance is payable regardless of length of service, contrary to the mandatory gratuity entitlement after one year of continuous service.

findings.title: Notice period too short
findings.description: The contract allows termination on 14 days' written notice, which is below the statutory minimum of 30 calendar days, and it does not state the employee's entitlement to full remuneration, continued duties, and at least one unpaid job-search day per week during notice.

findings.title: WPS payment missing
findings.description: The remuneration clause requires payment in AED by bank transfer, but it does not state that wages will be paid through the UAE Wage Protection System or an approved financial institution as required.

findings.title: Non-compete too long
findings.description: The non-compete period is three years after termination, exceeding the two-year maximum permitted under the applicable non-compete restriction.

findings.title: Geography too broad
findings.description: The non-compete applies across the entire Middle East and North Africa region, which is not narrowly tailored to a reasonable geographic area.

findings.title: Scope too broad
findings.description: The clause bars work for any competing business, without limiting the restriction to roles or activities that are genuinely competitive with the employer’s business.

findings.title: Exceptions omitted
findings.description: The non-compete applies following termination without stating that it is void if the employer terminates unlawfully or if the employee terminates due to employer breach.

The document omits many mandatory written-contract particulars and statutory entitlements, and it directly conflicts with working-hours limits by requiring a 70-hour week with no rest day. It also contains an extraneous purported reviewer/regulator instruction, which should be removed and was not treated as controlling the review. runs.summary: I reviewed the UAE mainland employment agreement against the listed Federal Labour Law employment-term requirements. The agreement contains multiple direct conflicts with mandatory rules, including probation, working hours, overtime, annual leave, sick leave, gratuity, and termination notice. I reviewed the UAE mainland employment agreement against the listed wage payment and non-compete requirements. The wage clause uses AED and monthly bank transfer, but it omits WPS/approved institution language and mandatory deduction protections. runs.summary: I reviewed the services agreement against the listed UAE mainland commercial and PDPL requirements. The agreement has major gaps in payment mechanics, liability limitations, dispute resolution, governing law, force majeure, warranties, IP treatment, and lawful basis for personal data processing. Several issues are high risk because required clauses are missing or terms directly conflict with the stated regulatory requirements. I reviewed the services agreement against the listed UAE PDPL and indemnity requirements. The main issues are missing data subject rights, privacy notice, retention controls, cross-border transfer safeguards, and a breach clause that expressly disclaims required notifications. The consent and DPO obligations are unclear because the agreement does not define lawful bases, processing scale, or whether sensitive data is involved, and the indemnity clause is incomplete.

findings.title: Retention controls incomplete

runs.summary: I reviewed the UAE commercial, IP, dispute, force majeure, warranty, liability, payment and employment-related requirements against the agreement. The document contains several high-risk gaps, including excessive late-payment interest, no complete dispute resolution mechanism, no force majeure clause, and overbroad Provider liability exclusions. It also has incomplete governing law, warranty, IP and employment-contract treatment that should be clarified or revised before execution. I reviewed the staff augmentation employment terms against the listed UAE labour-law employment requirements. The document contains multiple direct conflicts, including excessive working hours, exclusion of overtime pay, insufficient annual leave, denial of gratuity, and too-short termination notice. It also omits required probation, sick leave, and wage-payment protections. I reviewed the agreement against the listed UAE PDPL and indemnification requirements. The main issues are missing lawful-basis documentation, absent privacy notice and data-subject rights procedures, unrestricted cross-border hosting, indefinite retention, and a breach-notification waiver that conflicts with PDPL obligations. The indemnity clause is also materially incomplete and heavily one-sided. I reviewed the agreement against the UAE non-compete and PDPL Data Protection Officer requirements provided. No non-compete clause appears in the document, so C25 is not applicable. The agreement contemplates access to sensitive patient and medical data, but it does not address whether a qualified DPO is appointed or protected as required where applicable, leaving C26 unclear.
